title: The Creator Guide to Leaving TikTok for a Platform You Own (2026)
html:
TikTok is the best discovery engine on the internet and the worst place to build anything you want to keep. Those two facts are not in tension. They are the whole problem, and every creator eventually runs into it in the same order: the reach arrives, the money does not match it, and then one day the reach quietly stops and nobody explains why.

This is the country-agnostic version of our UK creator guide to leaving TikTok. Payout rates and tax rules differ by market. The structural problem does not, and it is the structural problem that decides whether the work you do this year still belongs to you next year.

DeHub is an independent DAO, co-founded by Mike Hales and Indi Jay Cammish, who also built First Class Agency, the United Kingdom's number-one official TikTok LIVE partner agency with more than 1,200 live streamers on its books. The people behind this platform spent years inside TikTok's monetisation machine. That is why this guide is specific about where the money goes rather than vague about it.

The three things you do not own

Your audience. Every follower is a row in TikTok's database. You cannot export the list, you cannot message it directly, and you cannot take it anywhere. When an account is restricted, shadow-limited or removed, the audience does not move with you — it simply stops existing from your side. Creators discover this at the worst possible moment, which is the only moment it ever gets discovered.

Your content. Your videos sit on TikTok's servers under TikTok's terms, surfaced by a ranking system you cannot inspect and cannot appeal. You are a tenant improving a property whose deed you will never hold.

Your rate. TikTok sets what a thousand qualified views is worth, does not publish the formula, and changes it without consulting you. The Creator Rewards Programme pays better than the Creativity Programme it replaced, but the eligibility bar is real — broadly around 10,000 followers and 100,000 qualified views in the trailing 30 days — and videos must run at least a minute to count at all. Reported rates vary enormously by market and niche, which is itself the point: any figure you read is a snapshot of a number somebody else controls.

Why "just move to another app" is not an answer

Most TikTok alternatives swap one landlord for another. The feed is different, the terms are the same: they host, they rank, they set the rate, and your audience is still a number in their database rather than a contact in yours.

The change worth making is structural. On DeHub, the decentralised social network, an upload is minted on-chain to your wallet at the moment you post it. That record is yours, independently of the platform. The feed is chronological and transparent rather than algorithmically opaque. The code is open-source, so no single company can quietly rewrite the rules underneath you.

If the whole category is new to you, our explainer on decentralised social media covers the mechanics without the jargon, and our roundup of the best decentralised social platforms in 2026 puts DeHub next to its peers.

What changes about the money

A revenue share you can read

DeHub commits up to 90% of ad revenue back to the ecosystem and the creators in it. The number is published rather than inferred, and there is no five-figure follower gate to switch it on. For anyone who has looked at a Creator Rewards dashboard and wondered why a quarter of a million views bought them dinner, a transparent majority share is a different sport entirely.

Attention that pays the viewer too

DeHub runs watch-to-earn bounties: you can attach rewards that pay viewers in crypto for genuinely watching. That pulls real attention rather than the hollow, algorithm-farmed impressions that inflate a view count without moving anything. Our pillar on what watch-to-earn actually is explains the model, and is watch-to-earn legit answers the obvious follow-up question directly.

Earnings settle in DHB, which lives primarily on Base, an Ethereum Layer 2, with contracts on BNB Chain and Polygon. It trades on decentralised exchanges and on Coinbase, and is listed on CoinGecko and CoinMarketCap. What you earn is portable and liquid rather than points stranded inside one app.

Subscriptions that keep paying after the sale

Subscriptions on DeHub are minted on-chain and are tradable, and when one is resold the original creator earns a royalty. A fan who backed you early can pass their subscription on, and you still earn from that secondary sale. It turns a monthly membership into an asset with a life beyond its first transaction — see tokenised subscriptions explained for how the royalty flows back.

One dial per upload, not one rule per platform

Every upload can be free, pay-per-view, or token-gated. A tutorial can be free to grow reach, a premium breakdown can sit behind a paywall, and a community drop can be gated to subscribers — all from the same account, decided per piece rather than by a blanket platform policy.

If live is your format

DeHub's live streaming runs on Livepeer and has scaled past 50,000 concurrent viewers, with on-chain streams and animated tips that land directly instead of being clipped on the way through. If you came up through TikTok LIVE, the gifting economics are the part worth comparing line by line — our guide to Web3 live streaming does that comparison.

The migration, in the order that actually works

Do not delete anything. A creator who burns their discovery engine to make a point ends up owning an audience of nobody.

  1. Claim your handle first. It costs nothing and handles are first-come. Doing this before you need it saves an argument later.
  2. Mirror, do not move. Post to both for a while. Your TikTok audience has no reason to follow you anywhere until there is something there.
  3. Give them a reason. Put something on DeHub that does not exist on TikTok — the full version, the unedited take, the thing that would be demonetised elsewhere. "Same content, different app" converts nobody.
  4. Point at it relentlessly. Bio link, on-screen mentions, end cards, pinned comment. Assume nine in ten people will not follow the link, and plan for the tenth.
  5. Move the money before you move the audience. Turn subscriptions on and set your revenue share up while your reach is still healthy, not after it collapses.

Treat TikTok as the top of the funnel and DeHub as the home base. That is the arrangement that survives an algorithm change, because only half of it depends on the algorithm.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best TikTok alternative for creators in 2026?

It depends what you are optimising for. If you want the closest clone of the TikTok experience, several exist and all of them keep the same landlord-and-tenant arrangement. If you want to own your audience, your content and your rate, you want a platform where uploads are minted to your wallet and the revenue share is published, which is the category DeHub sits in.

How much does TikTok actually pay per 1,000 views?

TikTok does not publish the formula, and the real figure varies by market, niche and audience composition. Reported Creator Rewards rates differ several-fold between countries. That variability is the reason this guide focuses on who sets the rate rather than on what the rate is this month.

Do I have to quit TikTok to use DeHub?

No, and you should not. Keep TikTok as your discovery engine and build your owned base in parallel. The creators who handle this well never announce a departure; they just gradually stop depending on one platform for everything.

What happens to my content if DeHub disappears?

Your uploads are minted on-chain to your wallet, so the ownership record does not depend on the platform continuing to exist. That is the practical difference between owning and renting, and it is why the minting happens at post time rather than as an afterthought.

Is DeHub only for crypto creators?

No. Payouts settle in crypto, but the content does not have to be about crypto — the platform carries video, music, live streaming, images and text posts across every category. The token is the payment rail, not the subject matter.
